Hitherto
hith-er-TOO
adverb
From hither (“to this”) + to; but where hither is of place — “to this spot” — hitherto is of time: “up to this point, until now.” The two must not be confounded.

Biblical Definition

Hitherto means up to now, until this time — and here a careful distinction must be kept, for the word looks like hither but does not mean it. Hither is of place: “come hither” is come to this spot. Hitherto is of time: it reaches back over all that is past and brings it up to the present moment. So the Lord defends His sabbath healing: “My Father worketh hitherto, and I work” (Joh 5:17) — the Father has been working, without ceasing, from creation until now, and the Son works with Him. The word is often the voice of gratitude looking back. Samuel raised his stone of remembrance and named it Ebenezer, “saying, Hitherto hath the LORD helped us” (1Sa 7:12) — every past mercy gathered up into one thankful monument. The children of Joseph plead their increase: “the LORD hath blessed me hitherto” (Jos 17:14), all the way to that day. And the porters of the temple are marked as those who “hitherto waited in the king’s gate eastward” (1Ch 9:18), faithful in their charge up to the time of writing. The word teaches the saint to read his whole past as a story of help. Hitherto — over every year and every trouble — the LORD has helped; and the God who has been Ebenezer thus far will not fail the little way that remains. What is behind is the pledge of what lies ahead.

Webster 1828 Definition

Up to this time; until now — of time, not of place (which is hither).

expand to see more

HITHERTO, to this time; until now; up to the present.

From hither + to; but the sense is temporal, not local.

Hither is “to this place”; hitherto is “up to this time.”

“My Father worketh hitherto, and I work” — from creation until now (Joh 5:17).

Samuel’s Ebenezer: hitherto hath the LORD helped us (1Sa 7:12).

Key Scripture

Joh 5:17 — "But Jesus answered them, My Father worketh hitherto, and I work."

Jos 17:14 — "And the children of Joseph spake unto Joshua, saying, Why hast thou given me but one lot and one portion to inherit, seeing I am a great people, forasmuch as the LORD hath blessed me hitherto?"

1Ch 9:18 — "Who hitherto waited in the king's gate eastward: they were porters in the companies of the children of Levi."

1Sa 7:12 — "Then Samuel took a stone, and set it between Mizpeh and Shen, and called the name of it Ebenezer, saying, Hitherto hath the LORD helped us."

Modern Corruption

A temporal word easily confused with the local hither; it recovers the saint’s backward look of gratitude — hitherto the LORD hath helped.

expand to see more

The trap in this word is not the age but the eye and ear: hitherto is so like hither that the two are readily confounded, yet they belong to different worlds. Hither is a word of place — come hither, bring it hither, to this spot. Hitherto is a word of time — up to this moment, until now. When the Lord says His Father worketh hitherto, He is not speaking of a place the Father has come to but of the unbroken labour of God from creation to the present hour. Confuse the two and the sense collapses.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the discipline of the backward look. Scripture teaches the saint to gather up his past into a monument of praise: Samuel set his stone and called it Ebenezer — hitherto hath the LORD helped us — not naming one deliverance only, but all of them, up to that day. This is the cure for the fearful heart. The God who has been our help in ages past, who has brought us over every flood hitherto, does not change and does not tire; His arm is not shortened for the road that remains. Faith reads the whole story of the past as help, and from that reading draws its courage for the future. Raise your Ebenezer, and go on.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

The word means up to this time, until now — of time, whereas hither is of place.

expand to see more

Hitherto — hither (“to this”) + to.

But its sense is temporal: “up to this time, until now.”

Hither is of place; hitherto is of time — do not confound them.

“My Father worketh hitherto” — from creation until now (Joh 5:17).

Hitherto hath the LORD helped us: Samuel’s Ebenezer (1Sa 7:12).

Usage

"Hitherto means until now: “My Father worketh hitherto” — from creation to this hour."

"“Hitherto hath the LORD helped us” — the whole past gathered into one stone of thanks."

"Mind the difference: hither is to this place; hitherto is up to this time."
